items.front: Kushanas — parent tribe and founder?
items.back: A branch of the Yuezhi (Yue-Chi) Confederation of Central Asia; empire founded by Kujula Kadphises I.
items.examPoint: Yuezhi (Yue-Chi) origin & spread into Gandhara/Kabul/Indus

items.front: Kujula vs Vima Kadphises — key difference?
items.back: Kujula I: founder, united Yuezhi, Roman-inspired coins. Vima II: gold coins, Shiva/Nandi devotee, expanded to Mathura.
items.examPoint: Vima Kadphises II — expansion to Mathura/Indus, gold coins, Shiva devotee

items.front: Kanishka I — accession year and its significance?
items.back: 78 CE — start of the Saka era (India's national calendar); Kanishka credited as its founder.
items.examPoint: Kanishka I — accession 78 CE, Saka era, empire extent

items.front: Kanishka's twin capitals?
items.back: Purushapura (Peshawar) in the north-west and Mathura in the Ganga-Yamuna region.
items.examPoint: Kanishka's capitals — Purushapura (Peshawar) & Mathura

items.front: Fourth Buddhist Council — patron, venue, president?
items.back: Kanishka; at Kundalavana near Srinagar (Kashmir); President Vasumitra, deputy Ashvaghosha; Mahayana–Hinayana split.
items.examPoint: Fourth Council venue Kundalavana; Vasumitra/Ashvaghosha; Nagarjuna

items.front: Which form of Buddhism rose under Kanishka, and its language?
items.back: Mahayana Buddhism; used Sanskrit; spread to China & Central Asia via the Silk Route.
items.examPoint: Rise & spread of Mahayana Buddhism; stupas & monasteries

items.front: Kanishka's divine title?
items.back: 'Devputra' (Son of God) — asserting the semi-sacred nature of Kushana kingship.
items.examPoint: Devputra title (Son of God)

items.front: Gandhara vs Mathura school — material & style?
items.back: Gandhara = blue-grey schist, Greco-Roman (Hellenistic) Buddha. Mathura = red sandstone, indigenous robust figures.
items.examPoint: Gandhara school — Hellenistic, blue-grey stone

items.front: Amravati school — material and patrons (contrast to Kushana schools)?
items.back: White marble-like stone, narrative Jataka reliefs; patronised by Satavahanas/Ikshvakus — NOT the Kushanas.
items.examPoint: Amravati school & Satavahana/Ikshvaku patronage

items.front: Match Kushana-age scholars to their works?
items.back: Ashvaghosha–Buddhacharita; Charaka–Charaka Samhita (Ayurveda); Nagarjuna–Madhyamika/Sunyavada; Vatsyayana–Kamasutra.
items.examPoint: Court scholars — Ashvaghosha, Charaka, Nagarjuna; Kamasutra; Greek astronomy

items.front: Kushana coinage — metals and standard?
items.back: Gold/silver/copper on the Roman standard; multi-faith deities (Shiva, Buddha, Zeus) → religious tolerance.
items.examPoint: Coinage — gold/silver/copper, Roman standard, multi-faith deities

items.front: Basis of Kushana wealth?
items.back: Control of the Silk Route → Indo-Roman trade + toll revenue; imported silk/spices, exported gold, gems, ivory.
items.examPoint: Silk Route control & Indo-Roman trade

items.front: Kushana provincial governor's title; administrative ladder?
items.back: Mahakshatrapa (chief satrap) → Dandanayaka (district) → Gramika (village); dual hereditary rule practised.
items.examPoint: Administration — satrapy/Mahakshatrapa, district & village officers, dual hereditary rule

items.front: Last significant Kushana ruler and who overthrew them in Central Asia?
items.back: Vasudeva I (early 3rd century CE, a Shaivite); the Sassanians overthrew them in Central Asia; India fragmented.
items.examPoint: Decline — Vasudeva I, Sassanian overthrow, fragmentation

items.front: Which chronicle records Kanishka in Kashmir, and where are his coins found?
items.back: Kalhana's Rajatarangini; coins/inscriptions at Mathura, Sravasti, Kausambi, Sarnath (Benares); Rabatak gives genealogy.
items.examPoint: Kanishka in the sources — Rajatarangini, coin-find sites, Rabatak

items.front: Which three regions did the Kushanas first dominate?
items.back: Gandhara, the Kabul Valley and the Indus Basin.
items.examPoint: Kanishka I — accession 78 CE, Saka era, empire extent
